passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
In order to "change lives for the better" and reduce "dependency," George Osborne introduced a new requirement for the jobless: the "upfront work search" scheme. Only if the jobless arrive at the jobcentre with a CV, register for online job search, and start looking for work will they be eligible for benefit and then they should report weekly rather than fortnightly. What could be more reasonable?

More apparent reasonableness followed. There will now be a seven-day wait for the jobseeker's allowance. "Those first few days should be spent looking for work, not looking to sign on," he claimed. "We're doing these things because we know they help people stay off benefits and help those on benefits get into work faster." Help? Really? On first hearing, this was the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better, complete with "reforms" to an obviously indulgent system that demands too little effort from the newly unemployed to find work, and subsidises laziness. What motivated him, we were to understand, was his zeal for "fundamental fairness" — protecting the taxpayer, controlling spending and ensuring that only the most deserving claimants received their benefits.

Losing a job is hurting: you don't skip down to the jobcentre with a song in your heart, delighted at the prospect of doubling your income from the generous state. It is financially terrifying, psychologically embarrassing and you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get. You are now not wanted; you are now excluded from the work environment that offers purpose and structure in your life. Worse, the crucial income to feed yourself and your family and pay the bills has disappeared. Ask anyone newly unemployed what they want and the answer is always: a job.

But in Osborneland, your first instinct is to fall into dependency — permanent dependency if you can get it — supported by a state only too ready to indulge your falsehood. It is as though 20 years of ever-tougher reforms of the job search and benefit administration system never happened. The principle of British welfare is no longer that you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment and receive unconditional payments if the disaster happens. Even the very phrase "jobseeker's allowance" is about redefining the unemployed as a "jobseeker" who had no fundamental right to a benefit he or she has earned through making national insurance contributions. Instead, the claimant receives a time-limited "allowance," conditional on actively seeking a job; no entitlement and no insurance, at £71.70 a week, one of the least generous in the EU.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
All around the world, lawyers generate more hostility than the members of any other profession — with the possible exception of journalism. But there are few places where clients have more grounds for complaint than America.

During the decade before the economic crisis, spending on legal services in America grew twice as fast as inflation. The best lawyers made skyscrapers-full of money, tempting ever more students to pile into law schools. But most law graduates never get a big-firm job. Many of them instead become the kind of nuisance-lawsuit filer that makes the tort system a costly nightmare.

There are many reasons for this. One is the excessive costs of a legal education. There is just one path for a lawyer in most American states: a four-year undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject, then a three-year law degree at one of 200 law schools authorized by the American Bar Association and an expensive preparation for the bar exam. This leaves today's average law-school graduate with $100,000 of debt on top of undergraduate debts. Law-school debt means they have to work fearsomely hard.

Reforming the system would help both lawyers and their customers. Sensible ideas have been around for a long time, but the state-level bodies that govern the profession have been too conservative to implement them. One idea is to allow people to study law as an undergraduate degree. Another is to let students sit for the bar after only two years of law school. If the bar exam is truly a stern enough test for a would-be lawyer, those who can sit it earlier should be allowed to do so. Students who do not need the extra training could cut their debt mountain by a third.

The other reason why costs are so high is the restrictive guild-like ownership structure of law firms. In most states, only lawyers can own a stake in a law firm. That isolates them from the pressure to make money rather than serve their clients. But it also means they cannot raise capital by selling shares to outside investors, which would make law firms more efficient.

In fact, allowing non-lawyers to own shares in law firms would reduce costs and improve service. Other countries, notably Australia and Britain, have started liberalizing their legal professions. America should follow.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
The US $3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year's award in March. And it is far from the only one of its type. As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years. Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs. These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.

What's not to like? Quite a lot, according to a handful of scientists quoted in the News Feature. You cannot buy class, as the old saying goes, and these upstart entrepreneurs cannot buy their prizes the prestige of the Nobels. The new awards are an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them, say scientists. They could distort the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research. They could cement the status quo of peer-reviewed research. They do not fund peer-reviewed research. They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.

The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism. Some want to shock, others to draw people into science, or to better reward those who have made their careers in research.

As Nature has pointed out before, there are some legitimate concerns about how science prizes — both new and old — are distributed. The Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, launched this year, takes an unrepresentative view of what the life sciences include. But the Nobel Foundation's limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research — as will be demonstrated by the inevitable row over who is ignored when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson. The Nobels were themselves once new and there is every reason to hope that the new prizes will also endure. Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy.

As much as some scientists may complain about the new awards, two things seem clear. First, most of the donors have their hearts in the right place. Second, the public is interested in science and in scientists; but it needs a little help to appreciate how and where to look. It is fair to criticize and question the new awards — and to make sure that they do not harm the culture of research. But these prizes are voluntary gifts from wealthy individuals who can do with their money as they please. It is wise to take such gifts with gratitude and grace.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
"The Heart of the Matter," the just-released report by the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (AAAS), deserves praise for affirming the importance of the humanities and social sciences to the prosperity and security of the nation. Dedicated to the comforting thesis that American education has in fact been built on the foundations of the humanities, the report sets out five goals: educated and integrative citizens, a vibrant workforce, a culturally vibrant society, research and innovation for global competitiveness, and nationwide leadership in international affairs. But the report's failure to address the genuine crisis facing liberal education may cause more harm than good.

In 2010, leading congressional Democrats and Republicans sent letters to the AAAS asking that it identify actions that could be taken by "federal, state and local governments, universities, foundations, educators, individual benefactors and others" to "maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific scholarship and education." In response, the American Academy formed the Commission on the Humanities and Social Sciences. Among the commission's 51 members are top-tier-university presidents, scholars, lawyers, judges, and business executives, as well as prominent figures from diplomacy, filmmaking, music and journalism.

The goals identified in the report are generally admirable. Because representative government presupposes an informed citizenry, the report supports full literacy; stresses the study of history and government, particularly American history and American government; and encourages the use of new digital technologies. To encourage innovation and competition, the report calls for increased investment in research, the crafting of coherent curricula that improve students' ability to solve problems and communicate effectively in the 21st century, increased funding for teachers and the encouragement of scholars to bring their learning to bear on the great challenges of the day. The report also advocates greater study of foreign languages, international affairs and the expansion of study abroad programs.

Unfortunately, despite two and a half years in the making, "The Heart of the Matter" never gets to the heart of the matter: the illiberal nature of liberal education at our leading colleges and universities. The commission ignores that for several decades America's colleges and universities have produced graduates who don't know the content and character of liberal education and are thus deprived of its benefits. Sadly, the spirit of inquiry once at home on campus has been replaced by the use of the humanities and social sciences as vehicles for publicizing "progressive," or left-liberal propaganda.

Today, professors routinely treat the progressive interpretation of history and progressive public policy as the proper subject of study while portraying conservative or classical liberal ideas — such as free markets and self-reliance — as falling outside the boundaries of routine, and sometimes legitimate, intellectual investigation.

The AAAS displays great enthusiasm for liberal education. Yet its report may well set back reform by obscuring the depth and breadth of the challenge that Congress asked it to illuminate.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Directions: The following paragraphs are given in wrong order. For Questions 41-45, you are required to reorganize these paragraphs into a coherent article by choosing from the list A-G to fill in each numbered box. The first and the third paragraphs have been specified for you in the table. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
[C] -> [A] -> [41] -> [E] -> [42] -> [43] -> [44]

[A] Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable — for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England. But these sites are exceptions to the norm. Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident. Olduvai Gorge, an early hominid site in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911. Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.

[B] In another case, American archaeologists Rene Millon and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the Valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City. At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world. The researchers mapped not only the city's vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.

[C] How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground? Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information. Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.

[D] Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes. In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copan, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural villages and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot. The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD 500 and 850, when Copan collapsed.

[E] To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques. Subsurface features can be identified without digging. Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features.

[F] Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them. Such searches can take years. British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun existed from information found in other sites. Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the Kings for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922. In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans combed antique dealers' stores in Athens, Greece. He was searching for tiny engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200s BC. Evans's interpretations of these engravings eventually led him to find the Minoan palace at Knossos (Knosos), on the island of Crete, in 1900.

[G] Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful. Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery. They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape. Archaeologists also use electronic sensing devices such as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detectors. Using computers to map the results of different surveys helps archaeologists visualize subsurface features without digging, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.

questions.stem: George Osborne's scheme was intended to ________.

options.text: encourage jobseekers' active engagement in job seeking
provide the unemployed with easier access to benefits
guarantee jobseekers' legitimate right to benefits
motivate the unemployed to report voluntarily

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】首段①句指出计划目的：使生活更好，并降低依赖。②句说明计划内容：失业者须带简历到求职中心、注册网上求职、并开始寻找工作，才有资格领取失业金；且之后须每周报到一次。结合两句可知，计划旨在鼓励失业者积极寻找工作、而不是依赖失业金，［A］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［A］结合②句计划内容，明确①句 In order to "change lives for the better" and reduce "dependency" 所述目的。
【错项排除】［B］对①句 change lives for the better 断章取义，由②句可知：获得救济是“更难”、而非“更易”。［C］对②句 Only if... will they be eligible for benefit... 反向干扰：该计划是在“限制”、而不是“保障”失业者领取救济金的权利。［D］用②句 they should report 干扰，但这属于计划细节、不能体现整体目的，且文中是“强行规定（they should）”、而非“鼓励自愿（motivate... voluntarily）”。
【技巧总结】本题考查“新政目的”，且直接定位信息为抽象概述，解题时需结合新政的具体规定、针对情形等加以理解把握，切忌断章取义。具体来看，答题时根据题干 was intended to 可直接锁定①句 In order to，并确定 change lives for the better and reduce dependency 为正确项来源。但由于该表述抽象概括，所以应结合②句“规定详述”加以理解，确定［A］正确。排除对直接定位信息断章取义的［B］，错误理解特殊句式（倒装条件句）的［C］，以及将“细节内容”当“整体目的”、且扭曲文意的［D］。

A passion to ensure fairness for taxpayers.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】根据题干设问直接定位至第二段⑧句（What motivated him...）。该句指出，激励奥斯本制定其计划的是对“基本公平”的热情：保护纳税者，控制开支，确保只有最应资助的申请者才能领到补贴。可见，［D］符合文意。
【命题解密】正确项是对第二段⑧句的概括：passion 近义替换 zeal，ensure fairness for taxpayers 概括 "fundamental fairness" — protecting the taxpayer...。
【错项排除】［A］源自第二段⑦句 the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better...，但这是表象（体现于 On first hearing），并非真正动机。［B］源自第二段④句 help people stay off benefits and help those on benefits get into work faster，但这是奥斯本自己的说辞，并非其真正动因。［C］对第二段⑧句 only the most deserving claimants received their benefits 反向干扰：新政明显是对失业金申请者“更小气”，而不是“更大方”。
【技巧总结】本题考查奥斯本实施新政的“真正动机”。解题关键在于：将文中信息分类、识别“表象”和“真相”。具体来看，解题关键在于将第二段信息分类：①②③④句介绍新政规定及奥斯本口中的“目的”（he claimed）——⑤⑥句作者发起质疑（Help? Really?）——⑦句作者说明表象（On first hearing）——⑧句说明真正动机（What motivated him, we were to understand, was...）。随后可排除来自于“奥斯本说辞”及“表象”的干扰项，留下来自“真正动机”的［C］、［D］。最后将两选项与⑧句仔细比对，排除与文意相反的［C］，确定与文意相符的［D］。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, being unemployed makes one feel ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第三段集中论述了失业带给人们的打击：经济窘迫，心理尴尬，感到不被需要，失去原有的目标感及有序感，无比渴望早日找到工作。可见，失业令人内心恐慌不安，［A］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［A］ uneasy 体现了第三段关键词汇 hurting... financially terrifying, psychologically embarrassing... not wanted... 表达的心理感受。
【错项排除】［B］ insulted 相关信息为 hurting，但根据①句冒号后及②句对其解释，可知失业带来的是心理窘迫难堪而非受辱。［C］ enraged 相关信息为 you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get，但从中无法得出失业者“愤怒”。［D］ guilty 无中生有，失业并非道德过错，文中未提及失业者感到内疚。
【技巧总结】解答情感态度细节题时，应从全段多处细节事实中提取核心情感基调，避免受个别极端情绪词（如 enraged、insulted）误导。整段描述失业造成的经济恐慌（financially terrifying）与被社会排斥感（excluded from work environment），uneasy（不安、忐忑）最准确中肯地概括了这种心理状态。

questions.stem: To which of the following would the author most probably agree?

options.text: Unemployment benefits should not be made conditional.
The British welfare system indulges jobseekers' laziness.
The jobseekers' allowance has met their actual needs.
Osborne's reforms will reduce the risk of unemployment.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段③④⑤句指出，奥斯本计划完全偏离了英国福利制度“无条件帮助人们度过危机”的建制初衷。福利制度本质上是一种社会保险，公民缴税正是为了在遭遇不测时获得确定无条件的保障。作者强烈反对给失业救济预设苛刻前提条件，［A］正确。
【命题解密】［A］合理推导了第四段主旨观点：作者借②句虚拟语气（It is as though...）及③④⑤句正反对比，论证失业救济金不应附加苛刻条件，与［A］完全吻合。
【错项排除】［B］源自第一段③句 state only too ready to indulge 及第二段⑦句 subsidises laziness，但这是奥斯本的理念（作者所批驳的看法）。［C］与第四段⑤句 no insurance... the least generous（救济金数目甚微，无法为失业者提供充分保障）相悖。［D］将第四段③句 you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment 偷换为奥斯本改革能够降低失业风险，与作者批判态度相反。
【技巧总结】推断作者观点态度题时，需准确区分“作者引述的反方/当事人立场”与“作者本人的批判立场”。作者通篇对奥斯本的新政持讽刺批判态度，认定失业救济应是社会兜底契约，不应设置惩罚性前置门槛。

questions.stem: A lot of students take up law as their profession due to ________.

options.text: the prospect of working in big firms

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】根据第二段②句“顶尖律师可挣得摩天大楼般高的钱，吸引众多学生涌入法学院（skyscrapers of cash... continue to lure in hordes of applicants）”可知，金钱回报是吸引学生从事法律行业的核心诱因，［D］正确。
【命题解密】题干 + 正确项［D］是对第二段②句 skyscrapers of cash... lure in... 的同义改写，the attraction of financial rewards 对应 lure in 与 cash。
【错项排除】［A］ the growing demand from clients 与第二段①句 clients... cut their legal budgets（委托人纷纷削减法律预算）相反。［B］ the increasing pressure of inflation 全文未提及通胀压力。［C］ the prospect of working in big firms 将大律所的高额收入偷换为去大律所工作本身。
【技巧总结】因果细节题直接锁定原文因果提示词（lure in 诱惑/吸引），将修辞化表达（skyscrapers of cash）转化为正规概括表达（financial rewards），即可迅速锁定答案。

questions.stem: Which of the following adds to the costs of legal education in most American states?

options.text: Higher tuition fees for undergraduate studies.
Admissions approval from the bar association.
Pursuing a bachelor's degree in another major.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第三段③句介绍当前法律教育体制：先要攻读四年非法律专业学士学位，后才可进入法学院攻读法律，最后还得花重金通过律师资格考试；④句指出这种教育体制的后果：给法学院学生带来巨大债务危机。换言之，③句所言三个因素为本题题干考查对象，而唯有［D］切合其中之一，故正确。
【命题解密】正确项对应第三段③句中 a four-year undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject。
【错项排除】［A］由④句undergraduate debts“本科债务”捏造出“本科学费更高”，而文中并未对比本科教育与法律教育费用高低；［B］由③句law schools authorized by the American Bar Association衍生出“接受专业协会的培训”，而文意实为“在美国律师协会许可的法学院学习”；［C］由③句for the bar exam“参加律考”衍生出“经得律师协会的准入许可”，而文意实为“律师资格考试费用高昂（而非准入许可）推高法律教育费用”。
【技巧总结】借题干隐性因果表达词adds to可知本题亦考查因果关联。解答步骤如下：首先根据题干关键词定位至第三段，搜寻到④句中因果表达词leaves，沿着其前This（回指③句内容）搜索至③句，发现句中实含三个因素（A then B and C），最后将三个因素与选项一一匹配可知［D］对应A。捷径：本题题干中adds to意表此题考查“增加的法律教育费用”，因此可先剔除与正常法律教育费用挂钩的选项，［D］中another major展示了这一深层含义，并对应③句中unrelated subject。

questions.stem: Hindrance to the reform of the legal system originates from ________.

options.text: the rigid bodies governing the profession
the stern exam for would-be lawyers

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段②句明确指出：切实可行的改革计划早已具备，但各州行业管理机构过于保守不愿推行（Sensible ideas... are around. But the state-level bodies that govern the profession are too conservative to implement them）。可见，保守僵化的行业管理机构阻碍了改革，［A］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［A］是对第四段②句的同义改写，其中 rigid 对应 too conservative，bodies governing the profession 原词对应 bodies that govern the profession。
【错项排除】［B］ lawyers' and clients' strong resistance 与文意相反，第四段①句指出改革对律师和客户都有益（help both lawyers and their customers），双方并不反对。［C］ the stern exam 是法学院毕业生的障碍，并非阻碍制度改革的根源。［D］非专业人士批评是推动改革的呼声，而非阻碍改革的阻力。
【技巧总结】细节事实题通过抓准主语施动者定位。题干 Hindrance（阻碍）同义对应原文 too conservative to implement them（过于保守而不愿推行），其执行主体正是 the state-level bodies that govern the profession。

questions.stem: The guild-like ownership structure is considered "restrictive" partly because it ________.

options.text: prevents lawyers from gaining due profits
bans outsiders' involvement in the profession
aggravates the ethical situation in the trade
keeps lawyers from holding law-firm shares

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第五段②句解释①句所述概念“限制性所有权结构”：除了哥伦比亚特区，非律师身份的人不允许拥有律师事务所的股份（non-lawyers may not own any share of a law firm）；④句也强调其本质是排除外部非专业人士准入（keeping outsiders out）。可见，限制性所有权排斥了外部人员参与，［B］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［B］是对第五段②句 non-lawyers may not own any share of a law firm 以及④句 keeping outsiders out 的同义改写，bans outsiders' involvement 准确对应排斥外部资本与管理者。
【错项排除】［A］ prevents lawyers from gaining due profits 与原文相反，大律所合伙人收益极其丰厚。［C］将律所借口维护职业道德（ethical argument）曲解为使道德恶化。［D］将限制“非律师（non-lawyers）”持股偷换为限制“律师（lawyers）”持股。
【技巧总结】考查段落核心概念的内涵界定。第五段采用“总（提出限制性所有权概念）—分（具体说明除特区外严禁非律师参股合伙）”结构，抓住 non-lawyers / outsiders 即可一击命中［B］。

questions.stem: In this text, the author mainly discusses ________.

options.text: the factors that help make a successful lawyer in America
a problem in America's legal profession and solutions to it
the role of undergraduate studies in America's legal education
flawed ownership of America's law firms and its causes

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】首两段提出话题“美国法律服务费用高昂”；第三段剖析教育体制与债务成因，第四段提出改革培训与准入的对策；第五段剖析行会式所有权垄断问题，末段提出开放所有权、引入外部竞争的对策。全文通过两个完整回合的“剖析问题—提出解决对策”展开论述，文章中心正是美国法律行业的问题与解决出路，［B］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［B］是对全文主旨脉络最精准有力的宏观概括，既涵盖法律服务昂贵低效之问题（a problem），又涵盖放开管制、引入竞争之对策（solutions to it）。
【错项排除】［A］由第三段教育路径捏造出成功律师的要素，偏离主旨。［C］将本科教育在法律培养中的环节这一局部支撑细节夸大为全篇主旨。［D］律所所有权结构仅为第五六段讨论的第二项具体问题，以偏概全。
【技巧总结】主旨大意题解题关键在宏观结构梳理。文章逻辑清晰：提出问题（首段高昂收费）→ 深入原因分析与对策一（教育改革）→ 深入原因分析与对策二（律所所有权改革）→ 呼吁美国效仿英国改革。问题与对策（problem and solutions）完美契合全文框架。

questions.stem: The Fundamental Physics Prize is seen as ________.

options.text: a symbol of the entrepreneurs' wealth
a possible replacement of the Nobel Prizes

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】首句开门见山指出 300 万美元的基础物理学奖（Fundamental Physics Prize, FPP）是个极具吸引力的尝试；②③句接着说明一系列类似的奖金丰厚奖项（lucrative awards for researchers）已加入诺贝尔奖之列，旨在奖励杰出科研工作者。可见，该奖项是对研究人员的丰厚奖赏，［B］正确。
【命题解密】［B］中 a handsome reward for researchers 是对原文 US $3-million、lucrative awards for researchers 的直接同义替换。
【错项排除】［A］利用首段④句 funded from the fat bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs 设伏，但这只是奖项资金来源，并非该奖项被赋予的社会认知属性。［C］过度推论，文中指出新奖与诺贝尔奖并存（join the Nobels），而非替代诺贝尔奖。［D］将银行账户（bank accounts）偷换为银行家的投资行为。
【技巧总结】首道细节题考查核心概念的定性。作者首段正面肯定新奖项设立的实质价值，抓住 lucrative awards for researchers（面向科研人员的丰厚奖项），与 handsome reward 构成标准近义替换。

questions.stem: The critics think that the new awards will most benefit ________.

options.text: the founders of the new awards

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】根据 The critics 定位至第二段前两句引入批评人士视角。④句尖锐指出：（批评者认为）设立巨奖实际上是背后设立者自我包装宣传的营销手段（The critics say... an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them）。因此在批评者看来，最大的受益者正是出资设奖的创始人们，［C］正确。
【命题解密】题干 + ［C］是对第二段④句 an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them 的合理推导，those behind them 即指设立奖项的创始人（the founders）。
【错项排除】［A］将批评者担忧奖项吸引心术不正者（skew the priorities）曲解为逐利科学家是最大获益者。［B］与第二段⑤句 time-honoured peer-review-led research 混合设置反向干扰。［D］同行评审研究体制恰恰是批评者担心会被新奖项侵蚀破坏的对象。
【技巧总结】观点推断题必须严格界定题目所问的主体立场（The critics think）。锁定原文 an exercise in self-promotion（自我推销的一场秀），其施动对象 those behind them 即对应 founders。

questions.stem: The discovery of the Higgs boson is a typical case which involves ________.

options.text: legitimate concerns over the new prizes
the joint effort of modern researchers

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段③句前半句指出，传统授奖对人数不超过三人的硬性限制早已与现代科研通力合作的性质严重脱节（the Nobel Foundation's limit... has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research）；紧接着后半句以希格斯玻色子的发现为例说明：这一发现是由数千位物理学家共同协作完成的。可见该案例体现了现代科研工作者的共同努力，［C］正确。
【命题解密】［C］是对第四段③句的合理推断，the joint effort of modern researchers 精准对应文中 collaborative nature of modern research 以及数千科学家的共同攻关。
【错项排除】［A］源自①句 there are legitimate concerns，但希格斯玻色子是用来举例证明科学协作性与旧评奖规则的冲突，而非新奖担忧。［B］将人数限制偷换为获奖者身份争议。［D］脱离段落论证核心。
【技巧总结】例证题的核心是“例子为观点服务”。希格斯玻色子发现案例紧跟在 the collaborative nature of modern research 之后，充当论据，论点即为科学研究已是集体智慧协作的产物，直接匹配［C］。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, which of the following is true of the Nobels?

options.text: History has never cast doubt on them.
Their endurance has done justice to them.
They are the most representative honor.
Their legitimacy has long been in dispute.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段④句指出，诺贝尔奖当年同样是由富裕的私人出资设立；⑤句紧接着指出：诺贝尔奖历经一个多世纪历史沉淀与时间考验，才确立了举世公认的合法性与尊崇声望（the Nobels have great prestige and history has given them legitimacy）。正是经受住了岁月的洗礼赋予了诺贝尔奖真正的崇高地位，［B］正确。
【命题解密】［B］是对第四段④⑤句内容的合理概括，endurance 对应历经岁月，has done justice to them 对应 history has given them legitimacy 彰显出其应得的声望价值。
【错项排除】［A］与原文不符：第四段论及新旧奖项均面临评奖机制局限性的质疑。［C］过度引申，文中仅称 have great prestige，并未断言为“最”具代表性荣誉。［D］将早年私人设立与评奖局限性曲解为合理性长期处于争议中，与末句肯定其合法性矛盾。
【技巧总结】事实细节题把握长难句的修辞与论证重心。作者强调历史沉淀（history has given them legitimacy）使得诺奖经受住时间检验，endurance 巧妙概括这一内涵。

questions.stem: The author believes that the new awards are ________.

options.text: harmful to the culture of research

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】首段①句 ...is indeed an interesting experiment 即奠定作者对新奖项“总体肯定”的基调；第二段虽列举批评者的担忧，但末段最终亮明作者核心立场：大方接纳此类新奖项是明智之举（It is wise to be grateful to the new awards...）；④句让步指出批评固然合理，但捐资人以自己的财富奖赏科研无可厚非，应予以包容接纳，［D］正确。
【命题解密】［D］是对作者综合态度的最合理概括。末段④句前半部分 It is fair to criticize 让步表明对外界批评的理解，对应选项 despite the criticism；后半部分以 but 转折提出捐资助研无可厚非，末句进一步肯定接纳新奖项，对应选项 acceptable。
【错项排除】［A］与作者首段及末段积极肯定态度直接矛盾。［B］源于第五段④句 it is the prize-givers' money to do with as they wish，但作者意在说明出资人有权支配资金，而非暗示奖项存在不良突变。［C］是第二段批评人士的消极担忧，并非作者立场。
【技巧总结】作为篇末作者态度题，解答需统揽全文论述脉络：作者虽承认批评人士指出的缺陷与铜臭隐忧（fair to criticize），但通篇主流立足于现实建设性视角，倡导积极肯定与感恩新奖项对科学界的注资扶持，因此“批评声中仍值得肯定（acceptable despite the criticism）”最精准体现了作者的辩证包容态度。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, what is the author's attitude toward the AAAS's report?
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】首段采取欲抑先扬手法：①句先肯定报告强调人文社科重要性的积极初衷（deserves praise for affirming the importance...）；②句转折词 however 引出核心论点：令人遗憾的是，该报告未能指出人文教育所面临危机的实质，结果可能是弊大于利（cause more harm than good）。可见，作者对其根本态度是批判性的，［A］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［A］是对开篇欲抑先扬、重心落于转折之后的批判性立场（cause more harm than good）的精准概括。
【错项排除】［B］ Appreciative 仅为①句表面赞扬的让步铺垫，并非作者最终定性。［C］ Contemptuous（轻蔑的）情感过度极端苛刻。［D］ Tolerant（宽容的）与文中明确直言其弊大于利、阻碍改革的鲜明批判立场不符。
【技巧总结】段落观点态度题需紧扣转折逻辑词。开篇赞扬（deserves praise）随即被 however（然而）与 cause more harm than good（弊大于利）强势反转，作者立意重在“抑”而非“扬”，态度确属 Critical。

questions.stem: Influential figures in the Congress required that the AAAS report on how to ________.

options.text: define the government's role in education
retain people's interest in liberal education
keep a leading position in liberal education

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第二段首句明确指出：国会重要人物要求 AAAS 拟定报告，界定各级政府及相关机构可采取的举措，以维持美国在人文与社科教育研究领域的卓越领先地位（to maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific scholarship and education）。可见国会的核心要求是保持领先地位，［D］正确。
【命题解密】题干 + 正确项［D］是对第二段首句 to maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific... education 的同义改写，keep a leading position 对应 maintain national excellence。
【错项排除】［A］、［B］、［C］利用首句中 actions taken by governments、educators、individual benefactors 等碎片词设伏，但国会要求的是界定“可以采取的行动”以维持领先，绝非要求界定“政府在教育中的角色”或“维护受教育权利”或“保持公众兴趣”。
【技巧总结】细节题直接根据题干核心词 Congress 和 required 定位至第二段首句。由 how to 明确考查行动旨归，快速定位末尾不定式目的状语 to maintain national excellence...，选项［D］直接完美对应。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, the report suggests ________.

options.text: an exclusive study of American history
a greater emphasis on theoretical subjects
funding for the study of foreign languages

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第三段②句详细梳理了报告提出的几项具体建议：支持全面扫盲、强调历史和政府体制学习，以及鼓励使用新的数字技术（and encourages the use of new digital technologies）。可见，应用新兴数字技术正是报告明确倡导的措施，［C］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［C］是对段中②句 encourages the use of new digital technologies 的标准同义改写，the application of emerging technologies 对应 the use of new digital technologies。
【错项排除】［A］利用②句 American history 设陷，但原文表述为 particularly（尤其是），而非 exclusive（排他的/唯独的）。［B］ theoretical subjects 全文未提及。［D］利用③句 investment in research 及④句 foreign languages 拼凑干扰，原文资助重点是教师培训而非孤立的外语学科研究。
【技巧总结】细节正误题需逐一比对选项修饰限制词。［A］将“特别强调（particularly）”篡改为“专属排他（exclusive）”，［C］通过词义泛化（use → application, new digital → emerging）实现同义替换，最为精准规范。

questions.stem: The author implies in Paragraph 5 that professors are ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第五段指出：现如今教授们惯常将进步主义的历史阐释和公共政策作为唯一适宜的研究课题，而将传统或古典自由人文思想（如自由市场和自力更生）描绘为超出常规、甚至超出正当合理的学术研究范畴（while portraying conservative or classical liberal ideas... as falling outside the boundaries of routine, and sometimes legitimate, intellectual investigation）。这实质揭示了教授们对古典自由人文思想抱有极深的偏见与排斥，［C］正确。
【命题解密】正确项［C］中 biased against 是对段中 portraying conservative or classical liberal ideas... as falling outside the boundaries of routine, and sometimes legitimate, intellectual investigation 批判态度的合理概括。
【错项排除】［A］与文意相悖，教授们将自由市场排斥在正当学术研究之外。［B］与原文相悖，教授们推崇的是进步主义公共政策（progressive public policy），而非保守主义。［D］曲解文意，教授们并非对学术研究谨慎，而是对特定人文思潮进行意识形态化打压。
【技巧总结】推断题需解读句群修辞与对比结构。该段核心句式为 treat A as B while portraying X as Y，对比体现教授对“革新政策（A）”的追捧与对“古典自由思想（X）”的污名化排斥，biased against 准确揭示其实质偏见。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.text: Ways to Grasp "The Heart of the Matter"
Illiberal Education and "The Heart of the Matter"
The AAAS's Contribution to Liberal Education

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】文首段点题：《问题的核心》虽值得赞赏，却未触及当前美国人文教育危机的本质（failure to address the true nature of the crisis）；第二段补充出台背景；第三至五段展开论述报告的致命缺陷：缺乏人文精神的非人文素质教育才是危机根源，而报告对此只字不提；文末段重申主题：报告遮蔽了问题的深度与广度，很可能阻碍人文教育改革。由此可见，全文核心是剖析非人文教育与《问题的核心》报告的关系，［B］最能概括文意。
【命题解密】正确项［B］是对文章主旨的最佳概括，精准融合文章评论对象 The Heart of the Matter 与批判主线 Illiberal Education。
【错项排除】［A］无中生有，文章重点在于批评报告缺陷，而非介绍如何理解该报告。［C］将首句让步肯定放大为文章核心，偏离全篇批判主基调。［D］仅涉及第五段论证局部，无法统摄全文。
【技巧总结】标题归纳题首尾呼应与双核心词法则。文章开篇与结尾均聚焦《问题的核心》（The Heart of the Matter）报告未能解决“非人文教育（Illiberal Education）”的实质危机，两者的矛盾冲突构成了整篇评论的核心框架，［B］最为贴切传神。

questions.stem: Choose the correct paragraph [A]-[G] for position (41):

options.text: Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable — for example, the Parthenon in Athens or the Colosseum in Rome.
In another case, American archaeologist René Millon spent decades conducting intensive surface surveys at Teotihuacán in Mexico.
How do archaeologists know where to dig? The simple answer is that they don't always know, relying on preliminary survey strategies.
Surveys can cover a single large settlement or an entire regional landscape to reconstruct ancient demographic patterns.
To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic ground reconnaissance and modern remote-sensing technologies.
Most archaeological sites, however, are undiscovered until modern building or agricultural work inadvertently exposes them.
Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint potential subsurface structures by systematically recording artifact scatters.

questions.explanation:
41.本题考查知识点：首段特点及作用
【选项推测】文首段通常用于引入主题或交代与主题相关的背景，内容相对独立，不应存在与上文 
相衔接的内容，也不应存在文意缺漏现象。纵观各段，［A］、［E］段已确定位置，［B］段段首In another 
case和［F］段首句however均体现与上文衔接关系，不能作为首段；而［D］段首句Surveys 一词指代不 
明，作为首段过于突兀。

【答案敲定】由上文分析可知，［C］、［G］段为备选项。
若［C］段为首段，可与［A］段构成“设问引题-铺垫背景”的逻辑顺序：［C］段设问引题“考古学家遗址 
搜寻办法”,并暗示指出“有迹可循条件下可肉眼观测，无迹可寻条件下则通过勘测及抽样（即试掘）方式”， 
［A］随后铺陈背景，明晰三种遗址发现方式（一、地表有迹可循，二、仔细搜寻，三、偶然发现），其中第一种完 
全对应［C］段nothing visible on the surface of the ground暗藏之意。另外,设问也是常用的开篇方法。
若［G］段为首段，那么与［A］段构成“地面勘测及其高科技手段-考古遗址三种发现途径”衔接。而 
仔细研读会发现,［G］段ground surveys应该涵盖在［A］段第二种方式“仔细搜查”当中，故排除。
